title: Blaze: Maintenance, Security Improvements, Testing & Assurances for the Blaze SDK

ms.promise:
・Fully implemented and validated chain providers (e.g. Blockfrost, Maestro)
・Utilities for safe and ergonomic chain interactions
・Fine-grained control over what providers are used for, i.e. separate providers can be used for querying, transaction evaluation, and transaction submission, with the potential for each specific query function to use a different provider
・Improved debug logging of provider interactions when needed, including the ability to show what API calls are being invoked and relevant params being passed
・Improved transaction building and submission API with more abstraction layers, including improvements to:
・Metadata handling
・Locking assets at scripts with type-safe datums and redeemers
ms.criteria:
・All major chain providers are functional and well-tested, at a minimum these are:
・Blockfrost
・Maestro
・Kupmios (Ogmios + Kupo)
・Transaction building API is intuitive and fully documented, and implements the primary features offered by other major tx building SDKs (Lucid, Mesh, e.t.c.)
・Testing suite passes with at least 80% code coverage of new features
ms.report:
A. Output: Fully implemented and validated chain providers, at minimum Blockfrost, Maestro, and Kupmios.
Acceptance criteria: Blockfrost, Maestro, and Kupmios are implemented, exported, and covered by provider behavior tests.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m1.md#provider-evidence
B. Output: Utilities for safe and ergonomic chain interactions.
Acceptance criteria: The SDK, query, and transaction APIs provide safer provider access, provider selection, transaction handling, and documented transaction-building flows.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m1.md#provider-evidence and https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m1.md#transaction-api-evidence
C. Output: Fine-grained provider control for queries, transaction evaluation, transaction submission, and specific query functions.
Acceptance criteria: Provider routing supports category-level routing and per-operation overrides for query, evaluation, submission, and specific provider operations.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m1.md#provider-evidence
D. Output: Debug logging for provider interactions, including invoked API calls and relevant params.
Acceptance criteria: Provider routing emits debug events so callers can inspect invoked operations, selected providers, params, results, and errors.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m1.md#provider-evidence
E. Output: Improved transaction building and submission API, including metadata handling and typed datum/redeemer script flows.
Acceptance criteria: The transaction builder supports metadata handling, typed script output locking and spending, provider submission flows, and governance/script redeemer builder paths.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m1.md#tran

ms.promise:
・Advanced chain querying functions, such as
・Websocket-based providers where on-chain events can be subscribed to and handled as they come in
・Ergonomic asynchronous setups where queries can be seamlessly chained
・Data caching and management systems
・Performance optimizations for large-scale queries
ms.criteria:
・Chain querying functions are comprehensive and performant
・Caching system effectively reduces network load

ms.report:
A. Output: Advanced chain querying functions, including websocket-based providers where on-chain events can be subscribed to.
Acceptance criteria: Chain querying functions are comprehensive and performant, and on-chain events can be subscribed to.
Evidence: The chain-event model is in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-query/src/events.ts. Websocket subscriptions run over Ogmios chain-sync in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-query/src/ogmios-chain-sync.ts, with a polling fallback for providers without websockets in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-query/src/polling-events.ts. Tests: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-query/test/ogmios-chain-sync.test.ts and https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-query/test/events.test.ts
B. Output: Ergonomic asynchronous setups where queries can be seamlessly chained.
Acceptance criteria: Queries can be chained cleanly through a single provider surface.
 Evidence: `CachedProvider` wraps any provider and exposes a `chain` helper for composed async queries: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-query/src/cached-provider.ts, tested in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-query/test/cached-provider.test.ts
C. Output: Data caching and management systems.
Acceptance criteria: The caching system reduces network load.
Evidence: TTL and size-bounded query cache with stable cache keys in https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-query/src/cache.ts. The cached-provider tests show repeated queries answered from cache without a second provider call: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-query/test/query-cache.test.ts
D. Output: Performance optimizations for large-scale queries.

ms.promise:
・Comprehensive test suite for transaction construction, which include:
・Unit tests of various methods
・e2e testing for full example transactions
・Property-based testing via fast-check
・Improved error messaging
・Safety features to minimise errors in tx building, including 
・Assigning datum/redeemer types to specific scripts, and throwing type errors when a passed-in datum/redeemer is mismatched
・Checking for accidentally reused transactions
・Minimising the risk of value being lost unintentionally by making any asset burns/transfers explicit
ms.criteria:
・Checks prevent common pitfalls in transaction construction
・Test suite covers edge cases and potential vulnerabilities
・Error messages are clear and actionable for developers
・No known security vulnerabilities in transaction construction
ms.report:
A. Output: Comprehensive test suite for transaction construction, including unit tests, end-to-end tests, and property-based tests using fast-check.
Acceptance criteria: Transaction construction is covered by unit, emulator-backed end-to-end, and property-based tests covering value conservation, asset preservation, minimum ADA, fees, determinism, mint and burn rules, metadata submission, and transaction confirmation. The tests and coverage command pass in CI.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m3.md#implementation-evidence and https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m3.md#verification. The passing public CI run is https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/actions/runs/29222021324 and the passing CodeQL run is https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/actions/runs/29222020922
B. Output: Improved transaction-construction error messaging.
Acceptance criteria: Common transaction-construction mistakes fail with specific errors that identify the failed operation and explain the invalid input or builder state.
Evidence: The implementation and tests are linked at https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m3.md#implementation-evidence. The documented error scenarios are at https://blaze.butane.dev/tx/guides/script-transactions#safety-checks-and-error-scenarios
C. Output: Datum and redeemer types assigned to specific scripts, with type errors for mismatches.
Acceptance criteria: Typed scripts bind their datum and redeemer types, typed locking accepts only the matching datum, and typed script inputs accept only the matching redeemer and unhashed datum.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-tx/src/typed-script.ts, https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/packages/blaze-tx/tests/tx/typed-script-types.test.ts, and https://blaze.butane.dev/tx/guides/script-transactions
D. Outpu

ms.promise:
・Comprehensive developer documentation and guides for using the Blaze SDK, including transaction building and chain querying, it will cover
・The base methods, functions, and relevant types
・Descriptions of each provider's implementation (so that developers understand what actual network requests are being made and how the providers work)
・Interactive tutorials and code examples using Aiken contracts, these will
・Showcase step-by-step how example transactions can be built with the Blaze SDK (with smart contracts built in Aiken)
・Demonstrate the different chain providers offered by the SDK and how to make queries with them
・These will be of a similar style and detail to the Aiken docs (https://aiken-lang.org/installation-instructions)
・Contribution guidelines and community resources
ms.criteria:
・Documentation covers all aspects of using and contributing to Blaze, specifically on building transactions with smart contract interaction.
・Afterwards, a new user should be able to write clean code which builds transactions with Blaze that interact with their own contracts
・The tutorials are accessible and cover key use cases, establishing Blaze as a solid tool for new developers to learn how to build on Cardano
・Community engagement tools are in place (e.g. issue templates, contribution guidelines)
ms.report:
A. Output: Comprehensive developer documentation and guides for transaction building and chain querying with Blaze.
Acceptance criteria: A new developer can follow the published guides from provider and wallet setup through transaction construction, submission, and chain queries.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m4.md#a-developer-documentation-and-guides and https://blaze.butane.dev/sdk/guides/developer-onboarding/
B. Output: Documentation for the base methods, functions, and relevant types used to interact with Blaze.
Acceptance criteria: Generated API references are available for the SDK, Blueprint, query, and transaction packages, with practical guides showing how the APIs fit together.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m4.md#b-base-methods-functions-and-types
C. Output: Descriptions of each provider implementation, including the network requests they make.
Acceptance criteria: The provider documentation explains Blockfrost, Maestro, and Kupmios request paths, pagination and resolution behavior, transaction submission and evaluation, script-reference lookup, provider routing, and caching boundaries.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m4.md#c-provider-implementation-descriptions and https://blaze.butane.dev/query/guides/provider-internals/
D. Output: Interactive tutorials and executable examples using Aiken contracts.
Acceptance criteria: The tutorial is backed by a runnable workspace that compiles an Aiken validator, generates its typed TypeScript class, and uses it in a complete transaction flow.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m4.md#d-interactive-aiken-tutorials-and-examples and https://blaze.butane.dev/sdk/guides/aiken-contract-tutorial/
E. Output: A step-by-step example of building Blaze transactions that interact with an Aiken smart con

A. Output: Final close-out report.
Acceptance criteria: A public report describes the completed SDK work, maintenance framework, Cardano integration process, verification, security results, releases, and community adoption.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m5.md
B. Output: Final closeout video.
Acceptance criteria: A public closeout video presents the project results and demonstrates the repository, documentation, test workflow, roadmap, and release process.
Evidence: https://youtu.be/kcnueDtdJ64
C. Output: Well-organized GitHub monorepo for Blaze.
Acceptance criteria: Public packages, examples, tests, API reports, and documentation have clear locations and task boundaries. Workspace dependency policy, build orchestration, and release configuration are checked in, and the Blaze SDK 1.0.0 release is available on npm.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/docs/catalyst/1200041/m5.md#repository-and-maintenance-framework and https://www.npmjs.com/package/@blaze-cardano/sdk/v/1.0.0 and https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/actions/runs/32112042350
D. Output: Public roadmap and task management system.
Acceptance criteria: Current, upcoming, and ongoing work is documented publicly, with concrete work tracked through GitHub Issues and a public issue form.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/ROADMAP.md and https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/issues

Acceptance criteria: Contributor guidance documents how protocol, network, SDK, and provider changes move from upstream specifications through package ownership, implementation, tests, documentation, review, and release. SanchoNet support provides a tested example of this process.
Evidence: https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-cardano/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cardano-integration-changes and https://github.com/butaneprotocol/blaze-ca
